title: Permanent loss carry-back for companies
headline: Companies with global income under $1b can carry tax losses from 2026-27 back against tax paid in the previous two years and get a refund.
summary: Companies that are not significant global entities can now carry back revenue losses against tax they paid in either or both of the two previous years, receiving a refundable tax offset capped by their franking account balance.
effectiveLabel: Losses from income years starting on or after 1 July 2026

history.note: Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 2) Act 2026, No. 71, Schedule 1

bigStat.caption: losses carried back against tax paid in the prior two years

shift.to: Carry back for a cash refund

before: Company tax losses could only be carried forward against future profits; the temporary carry-back ended in 2022-23.
after: Companies that are not significant global entities can carry back revenue losses from income years starting on or after 1 July 2026 against tax paid in either or both of the previous two years.
The result is a refundable tax offset, capped at the company's franking account balance.
exemptions: Significant global entities (annual global income of $1 billion or more).
Companies that have not lodged returns for the current year and the five previous years.

actions.text: Keep the franking account in credit: its balance caps the refund.
Make the carry-back choice in the company tax return for the loss year.
